summary: Charles B. Wheeler Downtown Airport (MKC) is a medium-sized general aviation facility situated just minutes north of downtown Kansas City, Missouri, along the Missouri River. The airport primarily serves corporate aircraft, private pilots, and flight training operations, functioning as a reliever for Kansas City International Airport. It is named after Charles B. Wheeler, a former mayor of Kansas City who championed the airport's development in the mid-20th century.
faqs:
Q: Does Charles B. Wheeler Downtown Airport offer commercial flights?
A: No, MKC does not serve scheduled commercial airlines. Kansas City International Airport (MCI) handles all commercial passenger service in the metro area, while MKC focuses on general aviation, corporate jets, charter flights, and pilot training.

Q: How far is MKC from downtown Kansas City?
A: The airport is approximately 4 miles north of downtown Kansas City, typically a 10-15 minute drive depending on traffic and route.

Q: What facilities and services are available at MKC?
A: The airport offers fixed-base operator (FBO) services with fueling, hangar rentals, aircraft maintenance, tie-downs, and flight schools. It also features a control tower and customs capability for international general aviation arrivals.

Q: Can passengers fly into MKC on private or charter aircraft?
A: Yes, charter and private flights can be arranged into MKC through various FBO operators, making it a convenient option for business travelers heading to the downtown area.
transport_tips: Reaching MKC is easiest by car via Interstate 29 or I-35, with quick access from downtown Kansas City in roughly 10 minutes. Ride-share services like Uber and Lyft are readily available, and taxi service is also accessible. Public transit options are limited, so renting a car or arranging ground transport in advance is recommended for visitors unfamiliar with the area.
local_tip: Because MKC is so close to downtown, business travelers can save significant time by using it instead of MCI for private aviation, and then walking or taking a short ride to nearby attractions like the River Market, Power & Light District, or the T-Mobile Center without dealing with highway congestion.
